messages:
emily: Heads-up — thinking about tightening canary/ingest traffic for new model intake. want to propose a small policy change to avoid noisy regressions leaking to prod users.
mike: SGTM. what specifically are you thinking? smaller canary qps or extra validation gates?
emily: both. current flow: 5% traffic routed to canary variant, bench smoke + golden fuzz. proposal: 0.5% initial, gated by quick SLO checks (latency/err rate/mean-token-cost) for 30m -> then 2% for 2h with expanded eval sample -> then full roll.
jia: 0.5% seems conservative but might be fine for large customers. do we have telemetry/alert coverage for short windows? cadence matters.
emily: ops-bot: can we get a runbook snippet?
```yaml
canary:
  phases:
    - name: initial-smoke
      qps_pct: 0.5
      duration_mins: 30
      checks: [latency_p99 < 600ms, error_rate < 0.5%]
    - name: staged-bump
      qps_pct: 2
      duration_mins: 120
      checks: [output-quality-diff < 0.7, token-cost-delta < 5%]
    - name: full
      qps_pct: 100
      duration_mins: 0
```

ops-bot: noted. will attach dashboard links and create a temporary alert group for the canary window.
mike: what about batchy workloads? small qps can inflate token-cost variance since batching effects non-linear. we should normalize by per-token latency and also monitor batch size distribution.
jia: +1. also add a metric for prefix-cache-hit-rate. new models with different sequence patterns can tank cache efficiency and look fine on token-level SLOs but cost explode.
emily: good call. add prefix_cache_hit_rate > 30% or at least a regression guard. and add a manual hold if quality regression detected by our eval harness (we run golden prompts subset).
san: one more thing — model variants fallback. if canary fails, route to previous stable automatically? that's how it's configured today but need to make the rollback immediate for first phase, slower for staged bump.
emily: exactly. immediate rollback on severe safety/latency fails; for minor quality drift, auto-fallback to stable while paging the owning team.
mike: UX: we should provide teams a short checklist when they request onboarding: expected sequence length distribution, preferred golden set, and whether KV-cache priming is applicable. reduces false negatives.
jia: agree. also recommend a recommended quantization profile (fp16/q4_0/etc) and note known kernel caveats in runtime for perf parity.
emily: i'll draft a short intake template and add to model-registry workflows. one open question: conservative cadence will slow time-to-availability. are we ok with slower rollouts vs risk of exposing regression?
mike: for tiered customers maybe accelerate. add a label in registry: entitlement=tier1 -> skip staged bump and go to 5% after initial 10m smoke.
emily: i'll make that opt-in flag. thanks. i'll post a short RFC summary and the intake template after this thread. tagging @mike and @jia for review later today. :thumbsup:
